title: Playing London's Empire Theatre: the band on stage
summary: The tour began in London, then Paris, Belgium and Germany; the band played the overture in the pit and hot jazz on stage after intermission.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So when you went to Europe with the show, where did you go?
That's what I'm telling you. That's the first stop was London. We went to Paris, Belgium and Germany. Four countries.
The Empire Theater, this is in 1923. That's right. Now did the band ever play on stage? Yes.

Every show we played after the intermission. Just played tunes? Yeah. Well, we had a special number. We did that in the pit. Did the overture, you know. Uh-huh. But we, they had a cabaret scene. And then after the intermission, the band left the pit and went on the stage. It was cabaret scene. Uh-huh.
What did you play on the stage?
You mean what type of music?
It was all hot music. That show was nothing. Nothing cool about that?
No. You mean you played, were you playing jazz?
How did the people like it? All right.
How did it go over? Very good. Very good. It was a library show. It was a very library. Uh, Jimmy Johnson wrote this old fashioned love on a boat. Oh yeah?
Gone over. Was that first in that show? No.
No. No. No. No. No. Thank you.
